sections.h2: How does property tax work in Mercer County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Mercer County splits the job among three offices at the courthouse complex on West Lexington Street in Harrodsburg. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value, the sheriff collects the bill, and the county clerk records liens and receives bills that go unpaid past April 15.

The sheriff's page says the office collects more than $8,000,000 in tax money each year, so the tax desk is a large part of its work. Homes inside Harrodsburg get an extra city bill, which is covered further down.

sections.h2: What is Mercer County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Mercer County covers about 249 square miles of land in the Bluegrass region of central Kentucky. It was formed in 1785 from Lincoln County, Virginia and named for General Hugh Mercer. Harrodsburg is the county seat, and Wikipedia notes it was the first city formally chartered in what was then Kentucky County. Burgin is the other city, and Salvisa is a census designated place.

Visitors come for Old Fort Harrod State Park, the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill with its 30 or more historic buildings, and Herrington Lake. The Louisville Southern Railroad reached Harrodsburg in 1888. Neighbors are Anderson, Woodford, Jessamine, Garrard, Boyle and Washington counties.

The Census Bureau lists 132 building permits for Mercer County in 2025, so some buyers will compare an older house with a new build.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about housing in Mercer County?
sections.html:
Mercer County counted 22,641 people in 2020, up from 21,331 in 2010, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 23,733. It had 10,824 housing units in mid-2025.

Details from the 2020 through 2024 survey:

  • Owners live in 75.9 percent of homes.
  • Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,373 a month in housing costs, and those without pay $497.
  • Broadband reaches 86.8 percent of households.
  • Mean travel to work is 27.2 minutes.
  • The county holds 90.9 people per square mile, well above the 30.0 to 35.5 in Menifee and Metcalfe.

sections.h2: Which Mercer County offices should you contact?
sections.html:
The county's own pages and the PVA site give these details.

  • Sheriff: tax bills and payments. 207 W. Lexington St., mail to P.O. Box 126, Harrodsburg, KY 40330, phone (859) 734-4221. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday, and a drop box serves after hours payments.
  • PVA: assessments and exemption forms. 207 W. Lexington St., P.O. Box 244, phone (859) 734-6330, same weekday hours.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and delinquent bills. Mercer County Courthouse, P.O. Box 426, phone (859) 734-6310.

The PVA site has a public property search with limited detail, and a paid subscription opens the full database.

sections.h2: Why do Harrodsburg homeowners get two tax bills?
sections.html:
A house inside Harrodsburg city limits pays the city and the county separately. The city of Harrodsburg bills its own tax, and the Mercer County Sheriff bills the county, state, library, extension, soil conservation, health and school taxes. City Hall says bills go out at the end of September.

For 2025 the city lists these rates per $100 of assessed value:

  • City of Harrodsburg: 0.063
  • Kentucky state: 0.106
  • Mercer County: 0.116
  • Library: 0.064
  • Extension office: 0.042
  • Soil conservation: 0.010
  • Health department: 0.050
  • Mercer County schools: 0.705

The city's own example turns a $200,000 assessment into $126 of city tax. Rates are reviewed each year, so use the rate on your current bill.

sections.h2: What are the Mercer County tax due dates?
sections.html:
The sheriff's page gives the following calendar for the 2026 bills, which is the statewide pattern from KRS 134.015 with the county's own wording for the later penalty.

  • October 1 to November 1, 2026: 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 to December 31, 2026: face amount.
  • January 1 to 31, 2027: 5 percent penalty.
  • After that: a 10 percent penalty, plus an extra 10 percent sheriff add-on fee for payments from February 1 to April 15.

All unpaid bills move to the county clerk at the close of business on April 15, 2027. If a bill does not arrive, the sheriff asks you to call the office. The bills come on a white postcard with a yellow strip, easy to mistake for junk mail.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Mercer County assessment?
sections.html:
Book a conference with the PVA when the tax roll is open for inspection, which begins on the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days under the state calendar. If the conference does not settle it, you file at the county clerk's office, stating the value you claim.

The three member board hears appeals 25 to 35 days after the inspection window, and its first day includes a review of recent sales of comparable homes. Anyone paid to speak for you must be an attorney, a certified public accountant, a licensed broker or appraiser, or another type listed in KRS 133.120, and must carry your written authorization. An employee of the owner also qualifies.

Mercer County mixes town lots, farms and acreage on one roll, so choose sales of homes like yours. A farm house on acreage and a town lot do not compare well.

sections.h2: Who can claim the homestead exemption in Mercer County?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, or who are classified as totally disabled, can claim it on the house they live in. The sheriff's page tells people in those groups to call the PVA at (859) 734-6330 to sign up if they have not already.

KRS 132.810 allows one exemption per residential unit and counts a mobile home as a unit. It also states that the assessed value cannot rise because of the value you write on the application. Disabled owners under 65 renew each year, with an exception for service connected totally disabled veterans and those found permanently disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

sections.h2: What happens if Mercer County tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The clerk creates a certificate of delinquency after April 15 and the property carries a lien. Interest runs at 1 percent per month, with a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee added. The Department of Revenue's worked example shows a $1,000 bill reaching $1,254 on transfer and about $1,611 once the first county attorney notice is out.

Sales to outside buyers run from mid-July. After one is sold, the owner deals with the buyer, who may add more fees. The county attorney handles payment plans before a sale.

sections.h2: What should a Mercer County seller know about the January 1 rule?
sections.html:
Tax ownership is fixed on January 1. The Mercer County PVA explains that if you buy after that date, the bill still goes out in the former owner's name until the next calendar year, though the office tries to mail a copy to the new owner from the recorded deed.

That affects every closing. A buyer who never receives the bill can contact the sheriff for it, and a seller should plan who funds the year's tax. If the house has an older bill at the clerk, ask the clerk for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Mercer County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay the Mercer County Sheriff at 207 W. Lexington St. in Harrodsburg, or mail it to P.O. Box 126. A drop box on the front of the building takes payments after hours.

faqs.q: Does the sheriff collect the Harrodsburg city tax too?
faqs.a: No. The city sends its own bill, and the county sheriff sends a separate one for county, state and school taxes.

faqs.q: When does the 2 percent discount end in Mercer County?
faqs.a: The 2026 discount runs from October 1 through November 1, 2026. Payment at face value is accepted from November 2 through December 31.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund of the homestead exemption if I applied late?
faqs.a: Yes. Under KRS 132.810, a person who qualifies after paying receives a refund of the tax on the exempt amount.

faqs.q: I bought a house after January 1. Who gets the bill?
faqs.a: The bill is issued in the former owner's name until the next calendar year. The new owner can contact the sheriff at (859) 734-4221 for a copy.
